title: The Adventures of Sam Spade
paragraphs: Dashiell Hammett's private detective Sam Spade, played most famously by Howard Duff, recounts hard-boiled cases filled with murder, deception, eccentric suspects, and sharply comic dialogue.

Hard-boiled detective series built around Dashiell Hammett’s Sam Spade, with a more comic and self-aware radio characterization. The frozen GRH set is a surviving-subset archive, not a complete 245-broadcast run, and contains two proven duplicate-audio metadata conflicts.

GRH documents the program through ABC summer series (July 12, 1946 to October 4, 1946) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], CBS regular series (September 29, 1946 to September 25, 1949) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], NBC Howard Duff era (October 2, 1949 to September 17, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC Steve Dunne revival (November 17, 1950 to April 27, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer on 55 recordings), [[person|howard-duff|Howard Duff]] (performer on 38 recordings), Steve Dunne (performer on 18 recordings), and Sandra Gould (performer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include private-eye investigation, theft, robbery and stolen property, money, valuables and financial motive, deception, impersonation and hidden identity, romance, jealousy and relationships, and murder and homicide.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar hard-boiled detective boom, Sam Spade character-rights litigation, Network migration from ABC to CBS to NBC, and 1950 Red Channels controversy and cast/sponsor break.
